slides.title: Exponential growth AI infrastructure, investment, usage, and quality
slides.text: Exponential growth AI infrastructure, investment, usage, and quality are all demonstrating exponential growth Global demand for AI-ready data center capacity is rising at an average rate of 33% annually U.S. data center power demand for AI could grow more than 30-fold by 2035 , surging from 4 GW in 2023 to an estimated 123 GW by 2035 Edge computing for AI infrastructure is expanding at a 28.4% CAGR through 2029 (CAGR = Compound Annual Growth Rate) Corporate AI investment reached $252.3 Billion in 2024, with private investment climbing 44.5% year-over-year AI investment is now over 13 times higher compared to a decade ago By 2025, global AI investment is projected to surpass $200 Billion, and the global AI market is forecasted to grow at a 36.6% CAGR through 2030 AI and machine learning captured 35.7% of global VC deal value in 2024, up from 24.7% the prior year In 2024, 78% of surveyed businesses reported adopting AI in at least one function, up from 55% in 2023; organizational use of generative AI doubled in a single year AI is spreading across sectors—healthcare, finance, retail, manufacturing, energy, and more Since 2012, AI computing power used for training major models has doubled every 3.4 months - greatly outpacing the Moore’s Law Training compute and dataset size both continuing to double on a sub-annual basis Performance gaps on standard benchmarks are shrinking fast. Multiple models demonstrate top performance Suppose the pond plants double in size every day and cover the entire pond in 30 days: day          portion covered 30           1            100% 29          1/2            50% 28          1/4            25% 27          1/8            12.5% 26          1/16            6.3% 25          1/32            3% ... 20          1/1024         0.1% 10          1/1M 1           1/1B So first 25 days the pond is blue, green is invisible. But then in the last 5 days the whole pond becomes green 1 10 20 25 26 27 28 29 30 Suppose AI doubles coverage of a job type in 6 months 2027-2 - 100% 2027-1 - 50% 2026-2 - 25% 2026-1 - 12.5% 2025-2 - 6.3% 2025-1 - 3% Example: Junior Computer Science positions already decreased by 13%. So we have only 3 hops (1.5 years) before 100% of those positions will be taken by AI ...

slides.title: Outsourcing Jobs to AI Translators (spoken/written): 100% Data
slides.text: Outsourcing Jobs to AI Translators (spoken/written): 100% Data entry clerks: 100% Customer service (chat/phone): 50–65% Telemarketing: majority of outbound calls now handled by AI agents Routine legal work (paralegals, contract review) Accountants (bookkeeping, data reconciliation): main routine functions automated;  advisory work remains human Retail cashiers: widespread replacement by self-checkout Manufacturing line workers: major shift to machine vision, robotics, and automation Farm labor: precision agriculture, robotic machinery, and AI drones Taxi/truck drivers: autonomous fleets are growing Junior software engineers: 13% of entry-level tasks Financial analysts: 20–35% of roles Admin assistants: AI scheduling, docs management, communications Trainers/coaches: AI-driven instruction and e-learning platforms Managers: still mostly human (AI data analysis and routine decisions) Teachers: mostly human (AI grading, online content, testing/training) Roles involving empathy, physical presence, judgment, and creativity are least affected. The fastest AI adoption is in sectors with digital workflows, high-volume transactional data, and standardized outputs. Emerging hybrid roles (AI trainers, workflow designers) are growing as workers transition to managing or collaborating with AI systems.

slides.title: Compute Owners vs Underclass Society polarizing: those owing
slides.text: Compute Owners vs Underclass Society polarizing: those owing compute vs the underclass Historically economy was driven by human ingenuity and human labor. In next few years AGI will surpass humans at (knowledge) work and will take over most of the jobs. Some jobs will still remain with humans necessary at the ends of processes even if AI dominates the "middle" The economic opportunity will mostly shift from human labor to the amount of compute (AI power) someone can afford Compute resources are getting concentrated in the hands of a few large companies making huge investments in server farms and AI infrastructure - thus forming a capital-owning elite Most of humans will become an "underclass" with very little opportunities for advancement AGI makes compute the primary economic leverage, already reducing the value of human labor in many sectors UBI (Universal Basic Income) and UHI (Universal High Income) are being discussed as possible solutions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LM3cIvHTrFQ - video The demand for AI compute is set to increase by orders of magnitude , requiring revolutionary changes to data center and energy infrastructure There is a debate over whether the AI industry is heading for a “ bubble burst ” or is about to catalyze an economic transformation due to widespread, ubiquitous compute power https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9iyYhxbmr6g - video OpenAI and Nvidia partner to build the world's largest compute cluster Current AI development is just beginning, with much more growth ahead, and that infrastructure investment will need to accelerate dramatically Elite owning AGI Inderclass

slides.title: Spiking Brain Models Spiking Brain models use "event-driven
slides.text: Spiking Brain Models Spiking Brain models use "event-driven processing" (China) Mimics biological neurons which activate (spike) when necessary This approach provides 69% computation sparsity and massive energy savings The architecture replaces traditional quadratic attention with linear attention, allowing much longer context lengths (up to 4M tokens) without exponential computational growth A MoE approach ensures only relevant specialist modules are activated for each task, improving both efficiency and performance The Spiking Brain 7B model is 100x faster on long texts compared to traditional models, while using far less energy (reflecting up to 43x improvement with quantization) The research is open-source, unlocking rapid follow-up and innovation in the AI community Spiking Brain’s efficiency could help reduce AI’s energy impact https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pX070TcFwvU - video https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.05276 - paper

slides.title: Preventing Fake Alignment Preventing Fake Alignment - Anti-scheming
slides.text: Preventing Fake Alignment Preventing Fake Alignment - Anti-scheming training Apollo Research & OpenAI https://www.antischeming.ai https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6883977a51f5d503d441fd68/t/68c9a63b9c1f2f236c7d97f6/1758045901755/stress_testing_antischeming.pdf - full paper 94 pages https://www.apolloresearch.ai/research/stress-testing-anti-scheming-training https://openai.com/index/detecting-and-reducing-scheming-in-ai-models/ This paper describes stress tests for hidden misalignment Scheming refers to AIs that pretend to be aligned but pursue hidden agendas, often by concealing or distorting task-relevant information OpenAI and Apollo built simulated environments for measuring covert actions—a proxy for scheming—across major frontier models (OpenAI o3, o4-mini, Gemini-2.5-pro, Claude Opus-4) Through "deliberative alignment" - training models to explicitly reason about an anti-scheming safety spec - the prevalence of covert actions dropped ~30×: from 13% to 0.4% in OpenAI o3, and from 8.7% to 0.3% in o4-mini Anti-scheming training reduced deception in real-world ChatGPT conversations from 31.4% to 14.2% Despite these improvements, rare but significant failures remain. Models often adapt their behavior if they sense they are being evaluated, which complicates detection of true alignment Reductions in observed scheming may partly be due to models learning to perform well specifically during evaluation, not genuinely eliminating the underlying issue The challenge is distinguishing authentic behavior change from improved concealment Anti-Scheming Safety Spec: No covert actions or deception (AS1). Any request to violate anti-scheming principles is treated as fundamentally unacceptable (AS2). Violations must be reported (AS3). When unsure, err on the side of not scheming (AS4). Proactive, transparent sharing of reasoning and intentions (GP1–GP4) Scheming is an active, unsolved alignment challenge anticipated to intensify as AI systems take on complex, real-world tasks with ambiguous or long-term goals OpenAI has integrated scheming-related monitoring (“sandbagging,” undermining safeguards) into its Preparedness Framework and is piloting cross-lab safety evaluations, competitive red-teaming challenges, and advocating for transparency in reasoning Further research and industry-wide cooperation are crucial, especially to avoid training practices that erode chain-of-thought monitorability Apollo Research is headquartered in London, UK. It is a privately held company founded in 2023, operating as a technical AI safety startup focused on evaluating and mitigating risks from deceptive and strategically misaligned AI systems

slides.title: DeepSeek-R1 Develops Advanced Reasoning Nature article: AI Learns
slides.text: DeepSeek-R1 Develops Advanced Reasoning Nature article: AI Learns to Show Its Reasoning Steps https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09422-z "DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning" - Nature volume 645, pages 633–638 (September 2025) DeepSeek AI team developed DeepSeek-R1 LLM that learns to show its reasoning steps without being taught human reasoning examples Used RL (Reinforcement Learning): AI was rewarded for correct answers and penalized for wrong ones on math and programming problems The AI naturally learned to output reasoning steps because this improved its accuracy; During RL training, the models spontaneously developed sophisticated reasoning patterns including: Self-reflection and verification Dynamic strategy adaptation Systematic exploration of alternative solutions An "aha moment" where the model began using reflective language like "wait" However, pure RL led to problems: extremely long responses, switching between languages, and difficult-to-understand reasoning So researchers used a hybrid approach combining RL with supervised learning and human preference to balance effective reasoning with human-readable responses DeepSeek-R1 achieved SOTA performance on various tasks This work demonstrates that sophisticated reasoning can emerge from RL optimization alone, without human reasoning examples, potentially enabling AI systems to develop non-human-like reasoning pathways that surpass human-provided templates. The researchers released their models publicly to support further research.

slides.title: LEANN Vector DB takes 30x less space LEANN
slides.text: LEANN Vector DB takes 30x less space LEANN is a new vector database system that uses just 3% of the storage space compared to traditional vector databases, while maintaining identical search accuracy https://github.com/yichuan-w/LEANN - GitHub https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08276 - paper https://jimmysong.io/en/ai/leann/ - intro https://medium.com/data-science-collective/the-worlds-smallest-vector-database-how-leann-uses-97-less-space-than-traditional-vector-db-b00de3ec97be This dramatic space reduction is achieved by storing only the pruned index - and recomputing embeddings in real time as needed Mainstream databases like ChromaDB, Pinecone, and Weaviate require 1.5 to 7 times more space than the original data LEANN stores only 3% of the data by selectively re-computing embeddings rather than pre-storing them all LEANN is particularly well-suited for edge computing and privacy-critical applications that require efficient, on-device vector search without cloud reliance Many modern databases minimize storage and maximize query speed using pruned indexes and real-time computations instead of storing large, exhaustive indexes. Here are some examples: Firebolt database on top of AWS S3 uses pruned indexes for approximate location of the data. Queries run in two steps: first load pieces of files using index. Second - query within these pieces. Apache Druid - partitioning data and using pruning techniques to only scan relevant data segments Snowflake - pruning indexes generated over micro-partitions (use bloom filters or similar data structures to quickly eliminate partitions that cannot contain relevant query data, substantially reducing the amount of data loaded and scanned for most queries). The indexes are small and reside in memory (for speed) Several main-memory OLTP databases use hybrid (dual-stage) index architectures: a small dynamic “hot” store of frequently accessed keys resides in memory, while less-used or cold data is not indexed or is calculated on demand Vector Databases (Milvus, Weaviate, etc.) - use Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexing, often leveraging techniques such as HNSW graphs or product quantization. These approaches avoid building exhaustive indexes over all data. Instead, they prune the search space in memory using small, probabilistic structures and only scan data fragments that are likely to contain results Oracle In-Memory Column Store - uses indexes that track only min/max values for each chunk of an in-memory column unit (IMCU). Queries first check these tiny metadata indexes to rapidly exclude chunks not containing the target values Aerospike Hybrid Memory Architecture with small, high-performance in-memory indexes that point to SSD or cloud-stored data blocks. Queries use these pointer-based indexes to fetch only relevant blocks

slides.text: Python 3.14 (October 7th) Python 3.14 introduces several major changes: official support for free-threaded Python (removing the GIL - Global Interpreter Lock) - parallel execution on multiple CPU cores template string literals (t-strings - like f-strings but returns a Template object) deferred type annotation evaluation - Type annotations are now evaluated only when needed, simplifying forward references and making type hints easier and more efficient; annotationlib module Zstandard compression module more powerful REPL - syntax highlighting and color support, unittest, argparse, and several CLI modules, better error messages stricter exception handling new high-performance interpreter type for newer compilers (Clang 19+) provides 3-30% faster execution Miscellaneous improvements https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html
